title: Multidimensional latency heatmap by model & route (streaming vs sync)
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Goal:
Build a set of Grafana dashboards and supporting tracing/metric instrumentation that surfaces multidimensional latency for Redwood inference requests by model and route, with an explicit breakdown for streaming vs non-streaming paths. The intent is to enable SREs and ML engineers to quickly triage regressions, compare model variants, and measure the effect of batching/KV-cache/quantization on p50/p95/p99 latencies.

Background:
Current dashboards aggregate latency at the service level and provide some model-level panels, but they do not make it easy to compare streaming vs synchronous request paths or to see fine-grained percentiles per route+model pair. We recently instrumented additional tracing attributes (model.name, route, streaming=true/false, deploy_version) in ENG-14230; this work depends on that being deployed to runtime.

Proposed deliverables:
- A "Latency Heatmap" dashboard that shows model x route grid of p50/p95/p99 with color scale, selectable time window and ability to toggle streaming vs non-streaming overlays.
- Per-route detail panels: percentile time-series (p50/p95/p99), request volume, error rate, and median token-generation time. Panels should support quick filters by model, region, and deploy_version.
- Tracing hook checklist and sampling guidance: ensure spans include attributes: redwood.model, redwood.route, redwood.streaming (bool), redwood.deploy_version, and trace_id propagation to downstream adapters.
- Example queries for Prometheus/StatsD/Datadog and SQL for our metrics warehouse to populate the dashboard and heatmap pre-aggregation job.
- Runbook excerpt describing steps to investigate spikes and automated alerts for deviations in p95 (> 2x baseline) or increase in streaming vs sync latency delta (> 100ms).

Instrumentation and metrics schema (implementation notes):
- Metric names (canonical): redwood.requests.latency_ms{quantile="0.5|0.95|0.99"}, redwood.requests.count, redwood.requests.errors, redwood.token.gen_latency_ms.
- Required tags/labels: model, route, region, streaming (true|false), deploy_version, customer_tier (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Traces: add a top-level span for request dispatch with attributes above. Ensure the streaming responder has its own span and records bytes_sent and first_byte_time.
- Aggregation: compute p50/p95/p99 at 1m granularity for dashboard heatmap and keep 90d retention for rollups in the warehouse.

Dashboard specifics (panels):
1) Latency Heatmap (grid): rows = model (top N by traffic), cols = route, cell value = p95 latency (ms). Overlay toggle to show streaming cells separately (split view). Hover shows p50/p95/p99, req/s, and errors.
2) Model Route Detail: time-series p50/p95/p99 with annotation for deploy_version changes and canary windows.
3) Streaming vs Sync Comparison: stacked differential chart that shows distribution differences and average generation time per token.
4) Top regressions: table of model+route with percentage change vs baseline and link to latest trace sample.
5) Alert panels: list active latency alerts and troubleshooting links.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement dashboard templates and queries in staging using synthetic traffic; coordinate with ENG-14230 to ensure attributes available.
- Phase 2: enable in production for top 25 model+route combos, run for 2 weeks, collect feedback from SRE/ML Eng.
- Phase 3: full production rollout and add pre-aggregations to warehouse for historical heatmaps.

Testing and validation:
- Add synthetic load tests (sync and streaming) to staging that exercise a mix of short/long sequences to validate percentiles.
- Validate trace sampling and that each heatmap cell links to a representative trace.

Risks & mitigation:
- High cardinality from model+route+deploy_version tags. Mitigate by limiting heatmap to top N models by traffic and using combinatorial rollups for historical views.
- Streaming instrumentation gaps: ensure streaming responder span is emitted even on early cancellations.

Success criteria (short):
- Dashboard available in staging and production displaying p50/p95/p99 by model+route with working streaming toggle.
- On-call can use links from heatmap cells to open traces within 2 clicks.
- New alerts detected fewer false positives after tuning thresholds in 1 week.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap dashboard deployed to staging with p50/p95/p99 cells and streaming toggle
Tracing attributes (model, route, streaming, deploy_version) present in 95% of sampled traces in staging
Prometheus/Datadog queries return p50/p95/p99 for top 25 model+route combos in production during validation window
At least one SRE and one ML engineer have validated the dashboard and confirmed trace links
Runbook contains triage steps and alert thresholds, and a follow-up task scheduled if thresholds cause >10% false positives
